definitions.gloss: to deceive, to trick, to fool, to delude
definitions.explanation: To deliberately mislead someone by lies, disguise, or manipulation. A literary or formal word for deception, carrying a stronger moral weight than casual words like だます.

examples.japanese: {人|ひと}を{欺|あざむ}いてはいけない。
{彼|かれ}は{巧|たく}みな{嘘|うそ}で{周囲|しゅうい}を{欺|あざむ}いていた。
examples.english: He had been deceiving those around him with clever lies.

examples.japanese: {世間|せけん}の{目|め}を{欺|あざむ}くために、{彼女|かのじょ}は{偽名|ぎめい}を{使|つか}っていた。
examples.english: She was using a false name to deceive the eyes of the public.

notes:
CONJUGATION:
Godan verb ({五段動詞|ごだんどうし}), く row.
- Negative: {欺|あざむ}かない
- Polite: {欺|あざむ}きます
- Te-form: {欺|あざむ}いて
- Past: {欺|あざむ}いた

TRANSITIVITY:
Transitive ({他動詞|たどうし}).

USAGE:
A literary and somewhat formal word. In everyday conversation, だます or {騙|だま}す is more common. {欺|あざむ}く appears frequently in novels, news, and formal speech. It often implies a moral judgment against the deceiver.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {人|ひと}を{欺|あざむ}く: to deceive people
- {世間|せけん}を{欺|あざむ}く: to deceive the world/public
- {目|め}を{欺|あざむ}く: to fool the eye, to deceive
- {自分|じぶん}を{欺|あざむ}く: to deceive oneself

SIMILAR WORDS:
- だます: to trick, to deceive (everyday, casual)
- {偽|いつわ}る: to falsify, to misrepresent (formal/literary)
- {誤魔化|ごまか}す: to fudge, to cover up (colloquial)
